title: What Forma is for
summary: The idea in one page.
text: forma helps you train, eat and recover while asking you for very little. you log what you did — a meal, a set, a weigh-in — and forma works out what to do next: today's session, your calorie and protein target, and when to rest. today. invented sample data. when to use it you want to train and eat well, but you do not want to plan every session and every meal yourself. you want a plan that comes from your own numbers, not from generic advice. you want your logs to stay on your phone, with no account to create and no tracking. step by step forma runs on a short daily loop. log what you did: a meal on fuel, a set on train, a weigh-in on today. apple health can bring the reading in from a connected scale, so you do not have to type it. open today and read the big card near the top. it shows the next thing to do. that can be a check-in, a session to start or resume, a meal to log, a weigh-in to add, or a rest day to call. tap the button on the card and do that one thing. the check-in asks how rested you feel, on a scale from 1 to 10 (exhausted to great). a session card takes you to train. a meal card takes you to fuel. come back the next day. your targets, the weights to lift and your rest days are worked out again from what you logged. good to know the first time you open forma, you see a short setup before this loop starts. after that, forma opens on today. at the top of today you see the date and a greeting. below it is the big card for the next thing to do. under the card are three rings: fuel for the calories you have left today, train for your session, and recovery for how ready your body is. under the rings is the weight card with your 7-day average, a small chart and an add weigh-in button. tap trend on that card to see the full picture on progress. near the top right are the gear button, which opens settings, and a speech-bubble button labelled ask coach. answering is part of the optional forma power extras; without it the button opens the plans. targets, session plans and rest days come from tested calculations that run on your phone. an ai never produces them. your data stays on this phone, with a backup in your own icloud. there is no account and no tracking. only the optional forma power extras (watch connection, online ai) use forma's server. decisions use your 7-day average weight, not a single weigh-in. your first reading starts the average. single readings are kept for the record. related the four tabs a day with forma your two coaches privacy: what stays where

title: The four tabs
summary: What lives where: Today, Train, Fuel, Progress.
text: forma has four tabs: today, train, fuel and progress. each holds one part of your day, so you always know where to look. today, with the rings for fuel, train and recovery. when to use it you are new to forma and want to know what lives where. you are looking for something — a log, a chart, the exercise library — and want to find it quickly. you turned a coach on or off and want to know what changed on screen. step by step here is what each tab holds. tap a tab name to switch between them. open today . it is your day at a glance. above the rings is the big card for the next thing to do: a check-in, a session, a meal, a weigh-in or a rest day. three rings sit below it: fuel (calories left), train (your session) and recovery. tap the fuel ring to open fuel, the train ring to open train, or the recovery ring to open progress. under the rings is your weight trend. open train . it holds today's session, your week, the exercise library and injuries. open fuel . it shows what you ate today, your target, your week, and supplements. open progress . it starts with your weight verdict and chart: a short line on how your weight is moving, and the chart behind it. below that is one card, your body & training, with strength, recovery, body and the fitness score. today in detail the top row of today shows the date and a greeting. the gear at the top right opens settings. next to it, a speech-bubble button opens ask coach, where you can ask a question about your training and eating. answering is part of the optional forma power extras; without it the button opens the plans. the weight card shows your 7-day average with a small chart. tap trend on it to see the full picture on progress, or add weigh-in to add a reading. if the morning check-in is due, it appears as the big card: slide to how rested you feel and tap save. good to know train appears when the training coach is on, and fuel when the diet coach is on. both are on to start with; change it in settings > coaches. each ring belongs to a coach: fuel to the diet coach, train and recovery to the training coach. with one coach off, its ring is not drawn. train and progress each have a clock button that opens history & reports: your past sessions and your reports. if a backup has been failing or missing for three days, a small dot appears on the gear. the details are in settings, under data & backup. related what forma is for a day with forma today's session weight and the 7-day average

title: A day with Forma
summary: A simple rhythm that gives the coach what it needs.
text: forma works best as a short daily rhythm: a check-in and a weigh-in when you can, meals as you go, your session when you train. none of it takes long. together, these give the coach what it needs to plan what comes next. when to use it you have set forma up and want to know what to do each day. you want the smallest routine that keeps your targets and sessions on track. you missed a few days and want to pick the rhythm up again. step by step forma has two coaches, one for training and one for eating. this rhythm feeds both. morning: open today. if the morning check-in is showing, slide to how rested you feel and tap save. tap add a note first if anything is worth remembering, such as poor sleep or pain. weigh in when you can. tap add weigh-in on today, or let apple health bring the reading in. a few readings a week is plenty. if you have no weigh-ins yet, the weight card offers use apple health. it reads your weight from health, so you do not type it twice. forma only reads. eat: on fuel, tap the plus at the top right (add food) and log each meal as you go. logging while the meal is fresh keeps the day accurate. train: on train, tap the start button on today's session card and log your sets. evening: on fuel, open the more menu at the top right (the three dots) and tap close today. if you do not, the day closes by itself at 21:00 as logged. each piece feeds a calculation. the weigh-ins build the 7-day average that your targets follow. the meals and sets fill the day. the check-in says how you feel. if you stop weighing in for a while, one new weigh-in restarts the average. good to know tip: missed a day? you can still add or change meals for the last 14 days. older days are read-only. the check-in is a slider from 1 to 10, with a word for the number you pick. the ends are marked exhausted and great. the note is optional. the weigh-in sheet starts from your last reading. nudge it to what the scale says and tap save weigh-in. if you already weighed in today, the button on today says update today's weigh-in. the big card on today shows the one best next action, worked out from your day. on a busy day, doing only the card is enough. if the plan says rest, the card offers call it a rest day, with train anyway underneath if you would rather train. left the app in the middle of a session? today shows it as in progress, with a button to resume the session. related weight and the 7-day average log food: search, scan or by hand today's session change or remove an entry

title: Setting up
summary: The first questions, and what each answer changes.
text: setting up is four screens the first time you open forma. it collects the few numbers the calculations need, then shows your plan before you commit to anything. it is not a sign-up. there is no account. your data stays on this phone, and nothing is created until you tap start my first day on the last screen. when to use it you installed forma and want to get to your first day. you want to know why each question is asked before you answer it. you are moving phones and want to restore a backup instead of starting fresh. step by step what are you aiming for? choose one: lose fat , hold where i am , or build . - not sure? choose not sure yet : forma starts you at maintenance and suggests a goal once you log a body-fat reading. - setting up a new phone instead? tap restoring a backup? here before you continue. continue to your numbers . first set units to kg · cm or lb · ft . then set your height and weight with the wheels. - rather than move the weight wheels yourself, tap use apple health to fill it in from health, or i'll weigh in later . set your birth date with the wheel and choose sex : male or female. - a note on the screen explains why they are asked: birth date and sex are used for the metabolism formula and your body-fat ranges only. - the continue button stays dim until every answer is filled in, and the reason shows in words on the screen. forma is for ages 13 to 100. on how many days can you train? , tap the number of lifting days a week you want to aim for: 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6. - not sure? pick what you can keep up; it adjusts to what you actually do. - if you would rather move on, tap skip for now (4 days) . if you only want the eating coach, open i only want the eating coach on this screen and switch on eating coach only . - training days are then skipped, and your calories use your normal daily activity. tap show my plan . the last screen, here is your plan , shows today's calories as a big number with protein, carbs and fat just under it, plus your first session after that. tap start my first day when you are ready. - to see the working first, open how we worked this out . - to change an answer, tap edit . your answers are kept. - to change which coaches are on, tap only want one coach? when you tap start my first day , three things happen: your profile and settings are saved, the weight you set becomes your first weigh-in, and the 14-day free trial starts. before that point, closing the app loses nothing. good to know note: every change is saved as you go. if the phone is shut off mid-way, opening forma puts you back on the screen you were on. tip: apple health fills the weight box with the newest reading of the last week. it asks for permission once, on that screen, and during setup forma reads nothing but your weight. > if you said i'll weigh in later , the plan screen says so plainly: your calorie target appears after your first weigh-in, and forma will ask for it on today. note: with the eating coach only, training is skipped entirely: the plan screen labels your calorie number every day , because your calories are the same every day. more questions arrive when they are useful, not all at once. a training-style card comes with the first open of train, a reminders card waits until after your first check-in, a one-line note about the trial shows on the first day, and a card about forma power appears from day 4 of the trial unless you dismiss it. dismiss or answer each one; none of them blocks anything. everything you gave can be changed later in settings . your goal is under profile & goal , and whether one or both coaches are on is under coaches . related what forma is for a day with forma core and power icloud backup and restore

title: Core and Power
summary: What is on your phone for everyone and what Power adds.
text: forma comes in two levels, forma core and forma power. you subscribe to one of them, monthly or yearly, and you can move between them at any time. both keep your data on the phone; the difference is only what talks to forma's server. core, for everyone core is all of forma on your iphone. nothing about it needs an account or a connection to forma's server. with core you get: both coaches — a training coach and a diet coach, each working from your own numbers. food search and barcodes — search foods, scan a barcode or type it in. the bundled food table works offline. your training log — sessions, sets, progression and rest, with every lift's history. apple health (optional) — weight, body composition, sleep, heart-rate variability and resting heart rate, read on your phone. icloud backup — a copy in your own private icloud, and one before it. power, the step up power is core plus three things, all delivered through forma's own server: garmin watch data — sleep, heart-rate variability and activities from your garmin, in your coaching. online ai help for meals and the coach — read a meal photo, estimate a meal you describe, and word the coach's messages. only when you allow it, and never with watch data. ask coach — ask your coach a question in your own words. everything else stays in place. online ai is your choice online ai help is off until you turn it on, and a sheet explains exactly what is sent and where before you can. you can switch it off again at any time. switching off takes effect at once, even for photos still waiting to be read. your watch data is never sent to the ai service. note: besides the online ai with power, the model on the iphone itself can read food photos where the phone supports it. that runs on the phone and sends nothing anywhere. core. power. when to use it you finished the 14-day free trial and want to know what to pick. you are being asked on today to subscribe (or to consider power), and want the short version. you already have a plan and want to move up or down. step by step open settings , then subscription . the screen shows where your trial stands: days left in the free trial, or if it has ended, what still works. tap see plans (once you have a plan, that row reads see all plans ). the screen opens with the title forma plans . pick core or power with the switcher at the top. each shows one short list of what is in it, in plain language. choose yearly or monthly from the plan cards. the price shown next to each option comes from the app store. tap the subscribe button at the bottom. its words name your choice, for example subscribe to core, yearly , or upgrade to power, yearly if you already have a plan. confirm with the app store. on a new phone, use restore purchases to bring your subscription back. manage subscription opens the place under your apple id where you can change or cancel. note: payment is charged to your apple id and renews automatically unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the period ends. you can always manage or cancel in settings on your iphone: tap your name, then subscriptions. what happens without a plan if the trial or a subscription ends, forma becomes read-only. what still works your history, charts and settings. export, backup, restore, and delete all my data . a workout you have already started can still be finished. what pauses logging new food, workouts, weigh-ins or check-ins. the coaches, reminders and widget updates. nothing you logged is touched, and subscribing again resumes everything where it left off. tip: you do not need to subscribe during the trial. everything works until the day the trial ends, and your history stays either way. a small reminder appears on today in the last few days; it never blocks anything. related setting up privacy: what stays where icloud backup and restore garmin data

title: Log food: search, scan or by hand
summary: Three ways to add a meal in seconds.
text: the add food sheet is how every meal reaches your diary. one screen gives you several ways in: search, barcode scan, or typing the numbers by hand. whichever you use, you always see the numbers on a check screen before anything is saved. adding food. when to use it you just ate and want the meal in your diary. you are holding a packaged food and want its numbers straight from the barcode. you are somewhere with no signal and need logging to work anyway. step by step on fuel, tap the plus at the top right, labelled add food . choose the meal with the meal button at the top of the sheet: breakfast, lunch, snack or dinner. a subtitle under the sheet's title reads logging to the meal you chose. pick a way to add from the row of buttons under the title. search tap search and type in search foods . your own and recent foods come first, then the bundled usda table (works with no connection), then packaged foods from open food facts (needs the internet, so its results arrive a moment later). tap a result. the check screen opens with a grams field filled to a sensible default. change it, or tap one of the quick amounts shown under the fields. check the protein, carbs and fat each item shows beside the grams field, and the total under the items. the calories are always counted from the numbers on the screen, not taken from a database. tap save to the meal you chose. scan tap scan and point the camera at the barcode. the first time, the phone asks whether forma may use the camera. it is used only while the scan screen is open, and nothing is recorded or kept. no camera, or the bars will not read? type the digits printed under the bars into the field (a barcode has 6 to 14 digits) and tap look up . forma looks in your own foods first, then in open food facts. when it finds the product, the same check screen opens. you always see the numbers before anything is saved. manual tap manual . a blank entry opens: type the name, the grams, and the protein, carbs and fat. the calories box is filled in for you from those three numbers, so they always add up. check it, then tap save to the meal you chose. good to know tip: logged this meal before? under repeat at the top, one tap copies the last time you logged it — items and all. under saved meals , one tap puts a meal you keep back in. note: photo and describe are two further ways in, and they need ai: apple intelligence on iphones that support it, or forma power. on a phone without either, tapping them shows what they need and offers search instead . search, scan and manual work for everyone. limit: open food facts is a shared database, so a product can be missing or have no nutrition figures. when that happens, forma offers enter it by hand . the food you type is remembered together with the barcode, so the next scan of the same product finds it. careful: a scan finds one product at a time. for a meal with several things, keep the check screen open and use add another item . items can be named, portioned or removed before saving. anything a photo or description read could not work out is listed as discarded rather than being dropped silently. offline logging works as normal: your own foods and the usda table answer with no connection at all. only the packaged-food results from open food facts wait until you are online. with search and scan, nothing leaves your phone but the words you type into a search, or the barcode. if a scan keeps finding nothing, see a barcode is not found . related saved meals and repeating a meal change or remove an entry your day target, and why it moves online ai help

title: Saved meals and repeating a meal
summary: Save a meal once and log it again with a tap.
text: a saved meal is a meal you logged once and forma remembered. the next time you eat it, one tap writes the whole line back into that day, so you do not search the same foods again. when to use it you eat the same breakfast most mornings and want it logged before the day starts. a dinner you cook the same way each week comes back again and again. you usually log the same foods together, and searching them one by one takes too long. step by step save a meal once log the meal the way you normally do (one way is a search; see log food: search, scan or by hand ). on fuel, find one of its lines in the day's list of meals, in the card headed today's meals . tap the three dots at the end of that line. tap keep as a meal . a note at the bottom of the screen confirms the save and shows the name it was saved under. the name comes from the foods on that line: two foods give "one and the other", three or more give the first food and a count. note: you also reach keep as a meal by tapping a logged line itself, which opens the entry, and tapping keep as a meal at the bottom of that entry. both routes save the same thing. log it again next time you eat that meal, open fuel and tap the plus at the top right ( add food ). tap your meal under saved meals . it is logged at once into the meal named under logging to , and a note with an undo appears at the bottom. saved meals are listed with the name, the calories and the protein. the ones you log most often come first, and the sheet shows the six most-logged. or repeat the whole meal repeating works without saving anything first: on fuel, a meal with nothing logged in it shows a repeat button with the calories of the last time you logged that meal. tap it, and the whole meal is copied into today, one fresh line for each line you logged then. in the add food sheet, a section named after the meal — repeat lunch , repeat breakfast — shows the same thing: the most recent day first, and more brings up the other recent days. good to know note: a saved meal is a copy of the line you tapped, with the foods and numbers it had at that moment. editing the saved copy never changes the day you logged first, and fixing that day never changes the saved copy. note: keep as a meal saves the one line you tap, with the foods that line holds. foods you logged as separate lines belong to separate entries, so each needs its own save. tip: a saved meal remembers what you ate, not when. pick the meal you want in the logging to menu on fuel before you open the sheet, so a usual breakfast can go back in as lunch. the meal button in the top right of the sheet changes it there too. limit: the saved meals and repeat sections show while the search box is empty or holds a single character. once you type two characters or more, they give way to search results. repeat looks back over the last 60 days, and only at days before the one you are on. related log food: search, scan or by hand change or remove an entry ways to log your food

title: Change or remove an entry
summary: Fix a portion, move a meal, delete a mistake.
text: a day's food record is not fixed once you save it. every logged line can be corrected, moved to another meal, or removed. your weekly numbers follow the change. when to use it you got a portion wrong, or left a number out. breakfast ended up logged as lunch. you logged the same thing twice, or logged food on a day you meant to skip. step by step fix the numbers on fuel, find the line under its meal. tap the line. the entry opens with its numbers. change the amount, or the protein, carbs and fat. the calories are counted from those numbers; there is no box to type them into. tap save changes . cancel throws your edits away. move it to another meal swipe the line to the left. tap meal . in move to which meal? , tap the meal it belongs to. you can also tap the three dots at the end of the line (or press and hold the line) and choose change meal . either way, only the meal changes: the foods, the numbers and the time logged stay as they are. remove it swipe the line to the left. or tap the three dots at the end of the line, or press and hold the line. tap delete (with the swipe), remove (in the menu), or open the entry and tap delete this entry . swiping the line all the way removes it at once. a message at the bottom of the screen offers undo for a few seconds. tap it and the line comes back exactly as it was. the same three-dot menu also offers edit and keep as a meal , so a day can be corrected or saved from one place; see saved meals and repeating a meal for that. close or reopen the day to close a day sooner, use the menu at the top right of fuel: close today for today, close this day for a past day. if fewer than two lines are logged, forma asks first. tap done anyway . a closed day shows a closed line with a reopen button. tap it to open the day again until you close it. good to know note: a day closes by itself at 21:00, if something is logged in it. the close item only appears on a day with at least one logged line that is not closed yet. a day with nothing logged is never closed, by hand or by itself. note: weekly numbers lean on closed days: when at least three of the logged days in a week are closed, only the closed ones are averaged, so a half-logged day does not drag the number down. until then, every day you logged is averaged. see your week . limit: you can log and change days up to 14 days back; older days are read-only and show what you logged with nothing to tap. step between days with the arrows at the top of fuel, and tap the date to open a calendar. note: moving a line keeps the time you logged it. the entry screen has no field for the time: a line keeps its clock time until you remove it and log the food again. only a line logged today carries the time you log it at; on a day before today, forma times new lines to that meal's usual hour. careful: undo disappears after a few seconds. after that, a removed line is gone for good. tip: the full three-dot menu is also available as a press-and-hold on the line, and voiceover users have the same actions as named actions on the row ( change meal and remove ). related log food: search, scan or by hand saved meals and repeating a meal your week

title: Your day target, and why it moves
summary: How the calorie and protein target is worked out each day.
text: your day target is the calories — and the protein, carbs and fat — your body is expected to use today, adjusted for your goal. it moves on purpose: a training day is weighted for the training, and it follows your body and your recent logging. you never type the number yourself. fuel: today's target and what is left. when to use it you want to know what the ring on fuel is counting down. the target changed in the last few days and you want the reason. it reads far too high or too low, and you want to check the inputs. step by step on fuel, look at the big ring: the calories left today, or the calories over once you are past the target. tap the ring, or tap energy & target at the bottom of fuel. read why this number : one plain sentence about what you burn on a day like this and where your goal takes it. on a training day, the line also names the rest-day figure. when the target moves because the day type did, it is recorded under coach decisions. under how today's target is set , the rows add up to target : resting burn + everyday movement , then exercise (or exercise (none today) ), then your deficit , your surplus or your pace (maintain) . a weekly nudge row appears once the weekly check has moved the base. to change your goal, tap change my goal . it opens settings > profile & goal. below, where you stand compares the day eaten with the target, and is logging adding up? compares what your logging predicts with what the scale did: days you closed count, today never does. how the number is made the target is worked out from plain, tested arithmetic on your phone. each part: resting burn comes from a standard formula (mifflin-st jeor), using your height, birth date and sex in settings > profile & goal and the 7-day average of your weigh-ins. a lean-mass reading replaces the formula when you have one. everyday movement adds 10 percent of the resting burn: the everyday part, before any exercise. exercise adds a typical session's cost: 250 kcal on a strength day, 350 on a run day, until forma has at least 3 of your own sessions to take the middle of. a day not marked as a rest day counts that session from the start, before you log it. a day marked as a rest day adds nothing. past 21:00, a day with no session logged counts as a rest day. once your watch reports today's session, its figure replaces the estimate. your goal moves the day by one fixed amount of calories from your average day: about 17.5 percent off to cut, nothing to hold, 12.5 percent on to eat up. on a cut with a body-fat reading, the deficit that reading gives is used instead of the percentage. the goal itself is decided from your measured body fat (see body fat and lean mass ); until you have one, you choose it in settings > profile & goal. the weekly check may move the base of the target once a week, and only with at least 10 days of weight trend and 10 days of logged food to judge. on its own it never moves the target more than 7 percent away from what it was a week ago. it never applies a change that means losing more than 1 percent of your bodyweight a week; it asks you instead. it never takes the base below your resting burn. its changes appear under coach decisions (history & reports, the clock button on progress), with an undo . a floor. the target never goes below your resting burn, or below the common least-to-eat guideline for the sex in your profile: 1,200 kcal a day for women, 1,500 for men. that guideline never lifts the target above what the day burns. when the floor holds the target up, why this number says so. the macros. protein is a fixed amount per kilogram of your 7-day average weight: 2.1 g per kg to cut, 1.8 to hold, 1.7 to eat up. fat is 27.5 percent of the calories; carbs fill what is left. so only carbs and fat move between a rest day and a training day; protein does not. a worked example amira is 34, weighs 62 kg, is 165 cm tall. her goal is to hold her weight, and she trains 3 days a week. input value resting burn 1,320 kcal everyday movement 10 percent of the resting burn goal offset 0 (holding) strength-day exercise 250 kcal day calories protein carbs fat rest day 1,452 kcal 112 g 152 g 44 g strength day 1,702 kcal 112 g 197 g 52 g forma's own wording for that strength day: "strength day: 1,702 kcal — rest days are 1,452." the 250 extra kcal on the training day do not change the protein — it stays at 112 g. the training-day extra goes to carbs and fat. good to know note: the target follows your 7-day average weight, not a single weigh-in. if a number looks off, check the weigh-ins: one typing slip, such as 780 instead of 78.0, moves the average. with no weigh-in in the last 7 days there is no target at all, and fuel says so. fix a reading under all weigh-ins on progress. note: with the diet coach on alone, there is no training split: the target uses a typical amount of activity and is the same every day. limit: the floor is not optional. for sam, a man of 88 kg set to cut, the target on a rest day is 1,820 kcal — the same as his resting burn — because the cut would otherwise have taken it under that. note: protein is a floor: clearing it is the win, and going over is never counted against you. calories, carbs and fat are budgets: over is the one to avoid. the number counts what you are over by, from the first calorie past the target. the colour turns amber only once you are more than 100 kcal past it. tip: is it much too high or too low? check the height and birth date in settings > profile & goal, and your recent weigh-ins — a wrong birth date or height shifts every number. a rest day being lower is by design. then see troubleshooting . a past day keeps the target it had that day; today is worked out again as your weight, your day type and your watch data change. you never type a calorie number. forma works the target out, and the goal — cut, hold, eat up — is what you change. related weight and the 7-day average body fat and lean mass your week troubleshooting

title: Your week
summary: The weekly view and the weekly check.
text: your week is a card on the fuel tab. it compares what you averaged in a week with what you were meant to average. the weekly figures are averages of several days, so one unusual day does not stand on its own. when to use it you want to know whether your protein came out where it should over a week, not just today. you closed a few days and want to see whether they added up to target. your weight moved oddly and you want to check whether logging and the scale tell the same story. you want to look back at earlier weeks. step by step open fuel and scroll down to the your week card, which sits below supplements. read the verdict line at the top of the card, once the week has three or more complete days. it says in one sentence how the week went. look at the chart. each week shows up to three bars, one each for protein (marked p), carbs (c) and fat (f), shown as a percentage of your target. a dashed line marks 100 percent. read the line under the chart. it says how many days out of the seven count, and whether the week counts days you closed or days you logged. tap details to see the four weeks, listed newest first, each with its protein, carb and fat percentages, its average calories against that week's target, and the dates it covers. at the bottom of details, the which days count section explains the basis in one sentence and shows the legend: protein met, on target, over, under. note: in details, a week with nothing complete says nothing complete to average. before your first week exists, the card says your week fills in as you log and points you to closing days (or letting 21:00 do it) so the chart can start. how the weeks are built each week is a rolling 7-day block. the newest one ends today if today is closed, and otherwise yesterday. a week that reads seven of seven always means seven closed days. details lists four weeks. what goes into the average is one definition of intake: your food entries plus the doses of any supplement you gave macros to, such as a protein shake. a shake counts in your week just as it counts in your day. limit: today counts in the newest week only once it is closed: until then the block ends yesterday. once three of your logged days are closed, only closed days are averaged, so a half-logged day never drags a number down. if fewer than three days are closed yet, weeks average every day you logged instead, and the card says so. reading the bars the colours follow fixed rules, restated at the bottom of details: protein counts as met from 90 percent of target. going over protein is never marked down. carbs and fat are on target within 10 percent. over that, the bar turns amber. under is shown in a quiet grey. the weekly check two checks run alongside the week view. both use the same rule about which days count: once three of your logged days are closed, only closed days count; until then, every day you logged. is logging adding up? on the energy & target screen, a card compares what your logging and burn figures predict your weight should do over a week with what the scale showed over those days. it needs at least four complete days before it can answer, and shows how many you have until then. when the scale has moved less than predicted, it says the gap usually means food going unlogged, and sometimes the watch over-reading your burn. when the scale is moving faster than predicted, it asks whether your target is steeper than you intended. the weekly calorie check. once a week, the calorie target itself is re-examined against how your weight actually moved. small moves are applied on their own, always with a sentence saying what changed. larger moves are never applied silently: forma asks first and states the reason. for example, you are losing more than 1 percent of bodyweight a week, or a move would pass your safety limits. nothing is applied below your calorie floor: the higher of your resting burn and the common minimum forma uses. if you have undone a calorie change of this kind twice, it asks first instead of repeating itself. tip: a week that looks under usually has a simple cause: days you logged but never closed. open those days on fuel and choose close this day in the … menu at the top right, or let 21:00 close them, and the chart rebuilds. related your day target, and why it moves change or remove an entry supplements weight and the 7-day average

title: Supplements
summary: Track what you take and what it adds.
text: the supplements section on the fuel tab is a list of what you take, with a one-tap dose. it keeps a record and lets a dose count toward your macros where it should. forma does not advise what to take or how much. when to use it you take something most days, such as creatine or whey, and want a record of it. you want a protein shake to count toward your daily protein target. you want a nudge on the days you forget a usual supplement. step by step open fuel and scroll to supplements . tap add a supplement . fill it in whichever way suits you: tap scan the barcode to read a packet, tap a name under common supplements , or tap type it in . where photo reading is set up and allowed on your phone, photograph the label reads the supplement facts panel. you check what it read before anything is saved. on the form, check the name , pick a kind (protein, creatine, caffeine, vitamin or other) and, if you like, type a usual dose : the field suggests "5 g or 2 capsules". leave the macros per dose (optional) fields blank unless the supplement has some. if what you type is not a number, the form says "use numbers only, for example 24 or 1.5." a protein supplement with nothing entered is treated as unknown, never guessed as zero. tap add and log the first dose . from then on, tapping the supplement's name on fuel logs a dose. the green number on it counts today's doses. note: doses are logged for today only. if you are looking at an earlier day, the list shows that day's counts but does not log new ones. what each kind does the form describes each kind in one line: protein : counts toward your daily protein target. creatine and vitamin : no macros. caffeine : timed against your sleep. other : no note, no special behaviour. more options per supplement press and hold a supplement's name for its menu: log a dose . when the supplement has a usual dose, the item names your usual dose instead. out of stock and restocked . marking one out of stock shows a short sentence about your record of taking it, and its row is dimmed until it is back. logging a dose while it is out of stock marks it back in stock. stopped , and take it again to restart a stopped one. undo last dose . remove (keeps history) . the supplement leaves the list but its past doses stay. if you scan or photograph a supplement you already have, forma does not add a second one. it offers to log a dose of the one you own, or, if the old one was removed, to add it again. note: the names under common supplements fill in a name, a kind, a typical dose and, for some of them, typical macros. they are typical values you can edit, not a recommendation to take them. limit: scanning a barcode or reading a label photo is an aid, not a check. the numbers are what you leave in the form, so correct anything that was read wrongly before you save. a reminder when you forget if you want a nudge when you have not logged a usual supplement: open settings, then reminders & notifications . open reminders and turn on supplements . it only reminds you when your usual ones are missing for the day. on a day you logged them, it says nothing. related your day target, and why it moves log food: title: Today's session
summary: What the planner gives you and how to start.
text: the train tab opens on today's session: what the planner chose for you today and what to do with it. train. when to use it you are at the gym, ready to train, and want the session. you want to know which muscles are rested and why today's plan is the plan. you want to train again today, or on your rest day. you left the app halfway through and want to pick up where you left off. what train shows from the top: today's session card : its name, a line with the length in minutes and how many lifts and how many sets, and a sentence on which muscles are rested and since when. if an injury you have logged changes today's plan, its line appears on the card. below it, this week shows the days you trained and one line on your sets. then two quiet rows: the exercise library and injuries . the injuries row is highlighted only while an injury is changing today's plan. the clock button at the top right is history and reports , for everything in the past. step by step tap start . the button carries the session's name, so you know what you are starting. the full list of lifts opens, each with its sets, its reps and the weight to lift. tap a lift to open it and log its sets. the weight and reps are filled in from the plan or from last time; change anything that was different. after a logged set, when a rest is due, a countdown appears at the bottom; when it ends, log the next set. no rest starts after the last working set of a lift. when you are done, tap finish . a confirmation asks whether to finish, and says how many working sets will be saved. confirm finish session . you get a short summary, including next , the session forma suggests after this one and when. tap done to close it. note: with nothing logged yet, finish works differently: instead of saving, it asks whether to discard the empty session. nothing is saved. leaving and coming back you can leave the app mid-session and come back. train shows resume session , with your clock still running, and inside the session the header shows the elapsed time and how many lifts are done. the phone stays awake while a session screen is open, so the clock keeps running. typed numbers survive even if ios closes the app. tip: not today after all? you can leave the session screen with the down-chevron at the top left and come back later; your logged sets wait for you. discard it from the session's menu only if you want it gone. overriding the plan tap why this session to see which muscles are ready, which are still resting and why. when the planner has nothing for you today, that screen also holds make today a rest day . want another session today after you have already trained? on the next card, or on a rest day, tap train anyway . a sheet states what this means and asks you to confirm, then the session is planned from how recovered you are today, not tomorrow. overriding a rest day this way clears the rest mark. if you are coming back from a break or an injury an injury that changes today's session shows on the plan as a line naming the area and how many lifts were swapped for today. in the session, the lifts that replace others say instead of the usual one. your very first session sets your starting weights. log what you actually lift, and every session after builds on it. if you have history in another app, you can bring it in so suggestions start from your real numbers. where you train, how long a session should be (45 to 90 minutes) and warm-up sets are in settings > profile & goal. the settings note says changes apply to the next plan. related log your sets the rest timer add, swap and reorder lifts injuries

title: Log your sets
summary: Weight, reps and the next set, with no signal needed.
text: logging a set is one screen: the weight and reps for the set you are on, and one button to press. it is built for the gym floor, where your hands are full and the signal is not worth counting on. logging sets in a session. when to use it you are between sets and want to write down what you just did without losing your place. the weight on the bar was not what forma suggested, and you want the log to say what really happened. your first session: what you log there sets your starting weights. the gym has no wi-fi and no bars. logging works the same offline. step by step from the session, tap a lift. its screen shows the lift's name, its muscle group and the equipment it uses, how many sets at which rep range, and the picture of how the lift is done. the active set — the first one not yet logged — is the big card in the list of sets. the weight and reps are filled in from the plan or from last time. change anything that was different. change the weight with the stepper. below it, three buttons — ±1 , ±2.5 and ±5 — choose how many kilograms one tap adds or takes away. on a barbell lift there is also a plates for … kg button that opens the plate calculator. change the reps with the stepper. on timed lifts, such as holds or carries, this box counts seconds instead. a lift that uses pauses shows a pause box under the reps. press log set 1 — then 2, 3 and so on. the keyboard never covers this button. when you log the last set of the lift, forma asks how many more could you have done? tap 0 (none), 1–2 (a couple) or 3+ (plenty). tap skip if you would rather not say. the rest timer starts after each logged set. there is no rest after the last set: the lift is done and you go back to the list of lifts. logged sets shrink into the list above the card. tap any set you have not logged yet to make it the active one. when a set you log is heavier than anything you have lifted before, it gets a pr badge. after the set the set where you answered shows a short line, such as 1–2 left , so you can see how close you came. while you pick numbers, the active set shows what you lifted for the same set last session. at the bottom of the lift, the last time card lists every set of that lift from your previous session. good to know another set adds an extra set after the planned ones. use it when you have more left than the plan asked for. warm-up sets come first when the lift has them. log them with log warm-up ; they are marked w1 , w2 and never count toward your volume, your recovery or your records. your numbers are saved as you enter them, and the log writes them down when forma leaves the foreground. if ios closes forma in the background, the numbers are still there. logged a set wrong, or answered the wrong thing? fix it afterwards: open history and reports , open the session, tap the set and change it. changes to the past flow into your next suggestion. if a set cannot be saved, forma says so with an alert called check the set , telling you what to fix. you need no signal anywhere in this flow. your sets are stored on the phone, and your icloud backup catches up next time you are online. the question after the last set of each lift — how many more could you have done? — is what lets the next session push a little harder or hold back. related today's session the rest timer plate calculator past sessions and reports

title: The rest timer
summary: The timer, the Live Activity and the Lock Screen.
text: after each set, forma counts down the rest at the bottom of every session screen. glance at the bar on the screen when forma is open, or at the lock screen when it is not. when to use it you have just pressed log set and want a countdown without opening a clock. you keep your phone in your pocket or armband between sets and still want to see the time left. you want a nudge when the rest is over, not an alarm to shut off. the countdown a slim dark bar pinned above the bottom edge shows rest , the time left, and two buttons: +15 adds 15 seconds of rest. skip ends the rest at once. a thin fill runs behind the bar so you can see at a glance how much of the rest is left. how long a rest is depends on the lift, and each lift's own header shows its rest time: lift rest warm-up sets 60 seconds lifts for core, lower back and calves 45 seconds isolation lifts (one muscle at a time) 60 seconds compound lifts (several muscles together) 90 seconds plans in strength mode double the last two. there is no rest after the last set of a lift: when it is done, forma takes you back to the list. when the rest ends forma open on the screen : you hear two short beeps and feel a tap. the beeps are mixed into your music, which dips for a moment and then comes back. phone locked, or forma in the background : a notification says rest is over and names the lift and the set. the first time, ios asks whether forma may send notifications. tip: no beep? turn the volume up. no notification? open settings in forma, then reminders & notifications , and allow them there. lock screen and dynamic island on a phone that supports it, the countdown also runs as a live activity while you rest. it shows on the lock screen and in the dynamic island, and names the lift you are resting from. the expanded island also shows the set. you can read the countdown without unlocking the phone or opening the app. when the rest ends or the session finishes, the live activity disappears. the rest timer belongs to the training coach. with the training coach switched off, no live activity runs. the live activity carries its own buttons: −15 and +15 to change the rest by 15 seconds, and skip to end it, so you can adjust the rest without opening the app. the today widget the live activity only runs during a session. to see forma on the lock screen the rest of the time, add the today widget. it comes in a small and a medium size for the home screen, and in circular, rectangular and inline sizes for the lock screen. it shows calories and protein left, your 7-day weight average, and what to do next. touch and hold an empty spot on the home screen, then tap the plus. search for forma, choose today , pick a size and tap add widget . tip: if a widget looks old, open forma once. it updates the widget whenever the app is open. good to know the bar appears on every session screen — the list of lifts and each lift's own screen — so you never lose it by navigating. added too much rest? on the live activity, −15 takes 15 seconds back; shortening it to zero ends it. on the in-app bar, skip ends the rest early. the notification names the lift and set you logged, so you know which lift to walk back to. missed the rest entirely? the next screen is waiting; nothing is marked as done without you. related log your sets turn a coach on or off troubleshooting

title: Add, swap and reorder lifts
summary: Change a session to fit the gym you are in.
text: you can change today's session: add a lift the planner did not pick, swap one out when the rack is taken, sort the list into an order that suits the gym, or drop a lift that does not fit your day. every change stays inside the session and keeps the plan working. when to use it the gym is busier than the plan expected and the bench is occupied. you want one extra lift that you have a soft spot for. two of the lifts are at the far end of the gym and you would rather do them back to back. you do not have the machine a lift needs, or it hurts today. add a lift in the session, tap the plus button at the top right. the sheet add a lift opens. search, or scroll: your recent lifts come first, then every lift grouped by muscle. tap a lift to add it. it joins the list for this session and forma opens it ready to log. if you have done the lift before, the weight box is filled from your history. equipment taken? open the lift, tap the three dots at the top right and choose equipment taken? . the sheet instead of <lift> lists lifts that train the same muscle with the equipment you have and nothing your injuries rule out. tap one. a confirmation asks swap in <name>? — tap swap it in . same slot, same sets. sets you already logged stay under the original lift, and the lift screen shows a short note ( before the swap: … ) so nothing disappears without a trace. if nothing else fits, the sheet says so: nothing else fits . reorder tap the … menu at the top left and choose reorder lifts . drag the handles to change the order. lifts you have already started stay where they are, marked with a small lock. tap done reordering . in the normal list you can also long-press and drag a lift, or take another lift's place by dropping it on top. with voiceover, the move up and move down actions are in the accessibility actions of each lift. remove open the lift, tap the three dots, then remove from today . a confirmation asks remove <name> from today? and reminds you that it stays in your library. this only appears while nothing has been logged for the lift. once a set is logged, the lift stays in the session: swap it instead, and the logged sets remain under the original lift. good to know reorder lifts is offered once at least two lifts are still unstarted. how to do it : tap the small picture at the top of a lift, or the three dots, then how to do it , for a larger picture and a short description. the picture moves between the start and the end position by itself; with reduce motion on it stays still and you tap it to switch. a lift with a coloured tile and an equipment symbol instead of a figure has no demonstration picture yet. everything else about it works normally. a swapped-out lift stays in your library; nothing is lost from your history, and past sets keep their name. forma remembers that you made the swap, which it uses when it plans your next sessions. pictures in forma are credited under settings > acknowledgements. related today's session log your sets injuries

title: Plate calculator
summary: Which plates to load for a target weight.
text: the plate calculator shows the plates to put on each side of a barbell to reach a weight, using the plates your gym has. load the bar right the first time, without doing the maths in your head. when to use it you are on a barbell lift and want to know which plates go on each side for the weight you are about to lift. your gym has fewer plate sizes than the full load needs, and you want the closest load your plates allow. you want the warm-up sets worked out as plates too, not only the working weight. you train in more than one gym, and the bar or the plates are different in each. step by step open a barbell lift in your session and find the weight box. tap the button under it named plates for followed by the weight in the box, in kilograms. the plates sheet opens. set the target weight at the top with the minus button and the plus button. each tap moves the target by 2.5 kg. check the drawing below the target: one sleeve of the bar, plates heaviest first from the collar, sized and coloured like real plates. read each side under the drawing: how many of each plate size go on one side, as count × weight , then a line adding up the bar weight, the plates and the total. tap use , which shows the loaded weight in kilograms, to put that weight in the weight box and close the sheet. if the exact weight could not be made, the button adds instead . when the plates cannot make it if your plates cannot make the target exactly, forma says so and shows the closest load, with how far it is under or over. when two loads are equally close, it picks the lighter one. the button then says instead , and using it puts the closest weight in the box. if the target is lighter than the bar itself, forma tells you the bar is already heavier than your target. nothing is added, the sheet says the bar is on its own, and the drawing shows the bare bar. bar and plates at this gym the gear button on the plates sheet opens gym setup : bar — a 20 kg bar, a 15 kg bar, or a 7.5 kg ez bar. lifts whose name contains ez, such as an ez bar or an ez curl, start on the 7.5 kg bar on their own. the bar you saved for your gym does not change. plates you have — tap the sizes your gym has. the full range is 25, 20, 15, 10, 5, 2.5 and 1.25 kg, plus 0.5 and 0.25 kg microplates. you count pairs of each size, and as many pairs as you need. the setup is saved for the gym you chose in forma, so each gym remembers its own. tip: set the plates once, when you first open the sheet at a new gym. every calculation after that uses them. warm-up steps below the plates, the sheet shows your warm-ups for this lift as loads. if today's session has its own, it shows your warm-ups . otherwise it shows a suggested warm-up ramp of up to three steps: about half the working weight for 8 reps, then 70 percent for 5, and 85 percent for 3. each step is rounded to the nearest 2.5 kg. a step that is not lighter than the working weight is left out. each step lists its own plates. warm-up steps are never counted as volume. good to know the button only appears on barbell lifts. machines, dumbbells, cables and bodyweight lifts have nothing to load, so they do not show it. the button reads plates for this weight when the weight box is still empty. the sheet opens at the weight already in the weight box for the set you are on. if that box is still empty, it starts at the lift's suggested weight. change the weight afterwards and the sheet picks it up next time you open it. the calculator works everything out on your phone. it needs no connection. the drawing shows one side. the total counts both sides, so load the same plates on each unless the sheet says the bar is on its own. related log your sets today's session add, swap and reorder lifts

title: Past sessions and reports
summary: Look back at what you did.
text: the clock button at the top of train opens history & reports: every session you have logged, the reports built from them, and the tools to correct the record. use it after training to check what you did, fix a mistake, or see where your lifts are going. when to use it you want to look back at a session: its lifts, its sets, and how it went. you logged a set wrongly, or skipped answering for a set, and want the record to say what really happened. you trained but forgot to log it, and want the day filled in. you want the longer view: sets per muscle, your lifts over time, your weekly reviews. step by step tap the clock button at the top right of train. the history & reports screen opens, with recent sessions at the top. tap all on the sessions card, which shows your session count, to open history: every session, grouped by month. tap a session to open it. a session opens on its summary, then its sets, grouped by lift. tap a set to correct it: change the weight or the reps, mark it as a warm-up, or set how many reps you had left. tap save . to remove what you logged, open the set and tap delete set . to delete a whole lift, use the three-dot menu next to it. to add a missed day, tap the plus at the top of history, labelled add a missed session . pick the day: today or any day in the last three weeks. tap choose a lift and enter its sets. back on history & reports, tap sets per muscle for this week's sets per muscle and the last 8 weeks, and your lifts for every lift with its best set. tap a lift to see its trend. if you already logged a session on the day you pick, the lift goes into that session. forma never creates a second workout for one day. a day with no session yet gets a new one, which shows without a duration because how long you trained is unknown. the reports history & reports collects more than sessions: sets per muscle — each muscle's sets this week, with the last 8 weeks charted. the screen notes that 10 to 20 sets a week per muscle builds muscle. your lifts — every lift you have trained, with your best set and how many sessions it appears in. tap one for its trend. weigh-ins and measurements — your body records. weekly reviews — one line per week on how it went. coach decisions — when the coach changed a target, why, with an undo where it can be reversed. which rows appear depends on the coaches you have on. the food diary row only appears with the diet coach on. good to know changing a past set updates your recovery readings, your next suggested weights and your insights. corrections keep the record right. deleting a session asks first, and it cannot be undone. forma warns you that it changes your recovery, your next weights and your insights. warm-up sets are shown but never counted as volume, recovery or records. most edits can be taken back for a few seconds with the undo bar that appears at the bottom of the screen. your first session sets your starting weights. once you have repeated a lift on two different days, its trend appears in your lifts. note: a deleted session is gone for good. if you only meant to remove one lift or one set, delete that instead. related log your sets today's session
