title: Bring your workout history
summary: Import sessions from another app so progression starts from real numbers.
text: forma can read a csv file of workouts exported from another training app, match the exercises to its own lifts, and add the sessions to your history. instead of starting from nothing, your suggested weights, volume and strength trends begin from your real numbers. when to use it you are moving to forma from another training app and want your past workouts to come with you. forma's starting suggestions should come from what you really lifted, not from a first-session guess. you have no export, but you know your last weight and reps for a few main lifts. get the file from the other app in your other app, look for something named export data , export workouts or download my data . it is usually in its settings or profile. choose csv (a spreadsheet file) if it asks for a format. save the file to files or icloud drive, or share it to this phone. step by step open settings in forma, then import workout history . you can also start from the train tab before you have any history: tap import workouts under today's plan. tap choose a file and pick the csv. forma reads the file on your phone; nothing is uploaded. if forma cannot recognise the file's layout, it asks which column is which. date, exercise and reps (or time) are needed. weight, set number, unit column, warm-up flag, time, distance and notes are optional. tap use these columns when you are done. check the preview: how many workouts and sets, the date range, the weight unit, and how the exercises were placed. if the file does not say whether the weights are in kilograms or pounds, forma asks once. check a weight you remember, then choose. under exercises , each name forma could not place needs a decision: match it to one of forma's lifts, keep it as its own lift, or skip it. forma remembers your answers for the next file. tap import , then done to see the workouts in history. the preview also asks about dates written in a way that can be read two ways, such as 03/04/2026: you choose whether the month or the day comes first. if you have no file on the import screen, enter my main lifts opens a short form. enter your last weight and reps for each of your main lifts, and roughly when you last trained them. leave a lift empty to skip it. bodyweight lifts need only reps. that is enough for a first week. good to know the import runs entirely on your phone. the file never leaves it. importing the same file twice adds nothing. sets forma already has are left out. the preview lists everything before anything is written. sets already in forma are left out, warm-up sets are kept as warm-ups, bodyweight sets are kept with no weight, and set notes are not kept. rows with no reps (cardio or time-only entries) are left out because they are not strength sets. imported workouts are marked as imported. they are ordinary workouts afterwards: you can correct a set or delete a session in history. changed your mind? tap undo this import on the result page. it removes exactly the workouts that import added, and nothing you logged yourself. a file larger than 200 mb is refused. that is far more than a workout log, so it is probably the wrong file. if the import fails, nothing half-finished is left behind. forma says so and offers to try another file. limit: importing adds workouts, so it waits until your plan is active. if your trial has ended, your history, export and backup are not affected — only the import waits. related past sessions and reports today's session ways to log training export or delete all my data

title: Injuries
summary: Tell the planner what to train around.
text: injuries is a list on the train tab for anything that hurts right now. you log an injury once, and the planner leaves out lifts that load that area and swaps in other lifts. the planner only avoids and swaps lifts. it does not diagnose anything, and it does not replace your physio or doctor. when to use it a knee, shoulder, back or other body part is injured, and you still want to train. you have recovered enough to train again and want a few lighter sessions first. something is managed with your physio's blessing, but certain movements must stay out of the plan. an old injury cleared up, and you want it off the list for good. step by step on the train tab, tap injuries . tap the plus button (add injury) at the top right. the add injury sheet opens. choose where the injury is: neck, shoulder, elbow, wrist or hand, upper back, lower back, hip, knee, ankle or foot, or other. if the area can be on one side, pick the side : left, right or both. pick a status : active, recovering or managed. set pain now with the slider, from 0 to 10. under avoid , switch on anything that should stay out of your plan, for example no overhead press, no deep knee bend or no heavy spinal loading. tap save . from then on, the planner skips lifts that load the area and swaps in other lifts. today's session says working around , and names the injury it is working around. good to know keep the list current, so the planner steers correctly. under how is it? , tap better , same or worse . if you tap worse on an injury that is not active, its status goes back to active. tap change status to move an injury through active, recovering, managed and resolved. the same menu has delete , which removes it entirely. active and recovering drop the lifts that normally load that area, along with anything you switched on in avoid . a check-in is due again after 7 days. managed means you are easing back on purpose: the area's normal lifts come back into the plan, and only the things you switched on in avoid stay out of it. resolved means it is over. forma can then plan a few lighter sessions to bring you back up, and the entry says easing back in with the count left. each session you finish counts one lighter session down. tip: set pain now to how you feel at the moment you log. the change between check-ins, not one number, shows whether things are moving the right way. the injury list stays on your phone, like the rest of your logging. related today's session add, swap and reorder lifts log your sets

title: Weight and the 7-day average
summary: Why one weigh-in means little and the average means a lot.
text: body weight can move by a kilo or so in a single day because of water, food and salt. one weigh-in tells you very little. forma works from the average of your last 7 days: a steady line that shows the real direction. weight and its 7-day average. when to use it you are cutting, maintaining or gaining, and you want to know whether the pace is right. one weigh-in jumped up or down, and you want to know whether to believe it. you want your calorie and protein targets to follow your real weight, not one morning's reading. step by step tap add weigh-in on today, or the plus on the weight card on progress. enter your weight and save. apple health can also bring weigh-ins in from your smart scale, so you never type anything. a worked example sam weighs 88 kg and is on a cut. sam weighs in each morning from 26 october to 8 november 2026. the average for a date is the mean of the readings in the last 7 days including that date. the first days therefore use fewer readings. date weigh-in (kg) 7-day average (kg) 26 oct 88.4 88.40 30 oct 88.0 88.40 1 nov 87.9 88.31 4 nov 87.5 88.04 6 nov 87.3 87.81 8 nov 87.1 87.60 on 8 november the average is 87.60 kg. a week earlier, on 1 november, it was 88.31 kg. that is a change of -0.71 kg, or -0.81% of bodyweight per week. single weigh-ins jump around by half a kilo or more (88.9 one day, 88.1 the next), while the average moves smoothly. forma puts your pace against a band, in percent of bodyweight per week: goal aim band (% per week) cut -0.75 to -0.50 maintain -0.25 to +0.25 bulk +0.25 to +0.50 at -0.81, sam's week is just past the fast end of the cut band, so the verdict at the top of progress reads faster than aim . good to know on the weight card, dots are single weigh-ins and the line is the 7-day average. single weigh-ins are for the record. decisions use the average. the verdict depends on your goal. on a cut, it can read on track, faster than aim, too fast, slower than aim, stalled, or moving the wrong way. a loss faster than 1% of bodyweight per week crosses the "too fast" line, where muscle starts to go. changes smaller than about 0.1% per week count as flat. the average moves your calorie and protein targets. it also feeds the verdict at the top of progress, which compares your pace per week with the pace you aim for. if you go a week without a weigh-in, there is no current average until you add one. one new weigh-in restarts it. forma stores one weigh-in per day. if a scale reading and a hand-entered value both come in for the same day, the newer one takes its place. the average is worked out again from your full history each time you look at it, so it can never drift. every two weeks, forma checks what actually changed against what it predicted, and can raise or lower your daily calories. if the trend is inside half a kilo of what was predicted, it leaves your targets alone. tip: weigh at a similar time, for example after the toilet and before breakfast. several times a week works better than once. note: if you are losing or gaining weight faster than expected and feel unwell, see a doctor. related your day target, and why it moves body fat and lean mass ways to judge progress apple health

title: Body fat and lean mass
summary: Reading body composition.
text: your weight says how heavy you are. body fat and lean mass say what the weight is made of. the body row on progress opens this screen. it shows readings from apple health, clinic scans you add, and an estimate from your tape measurements. it also shows the goal your body fat points to. when to use it you are losing weight and want to know whether you are losing fat or muscle. you have had a clinic scan, such as a dexa, and want the result to shape your plan. you want to see why your goal is cut, hold or eat up, and how it was worked out. your smart scale disagrees with your clinic scans, and you want to know which to trust. step by step on progress, tap the body row. if you have a scan result you want to keep, tap add a clinic scan and enter it. tap why this goal to see your body fat range and how your goal follows from it. good to know until you have any measurement, you choose your goal yourself in settings. how your goal is decided. when you have body fat readings, the goal is decided from your body fat against a range that depends on your sex: sex eat up (gain) hold cut women under 18% 18 to 23% over 23% men under 10% 10 to 15% over 15% eat up means the plan targets a surplus, hold means maintenance, and cut means a deficit. tap why this goal to see your own numbers instead of these general bands. what two readings can tell you. between two readings, forma works out how your lean mass and your fat changed, and can cross-check that against your training: if lean mass goes up while fat goes down, that reads as recomposition : you added muscle and lost fat in the same period. if the change is under about 0.7 kg of lean mass or 1 fat point, the read is holding . these devices cannot resolve changes smaller than that. the other verdicts are fat down , fat up and lean mass down . forma also checks the change against your lifts: it compares your estimated one-rep maxes on lifts you did in both periods. early strength gains often come from practice rather than muscle, so a falling strength trend is the strongest independent confirmation. a scale or a clinic scan is preferred. the tape estimate is only a second opinion. a clinic scan you add yourself is never overwritten by automatic readings. later readings from a scale or apple health replace earlier non-clinic entries for the same day, so your scans stay put. apple health can send body fat and lean mass readings from your smart scale into forma. if more than one automatic reading lands on the same day, the one taken latest wins. tip: read the direction over several weeks, not the exact level. different devices read differently, so keep using the same one. limit: a smart scale's body fat estimate in particular carries a wide margin of error. treat every reading here as an estimate, not a measurement you can rely on. related weight and the 7-day average tape measurements your day target, and why it moves ways to judge progress

title: Strength
summary: How your lifts are moving.
text: the strength screen shows how your lifts are moving and how much work each muscle is getting. it works from the sessions you log in the train tab. when to use it after a few weeks of logging sets, to see which lifts are going up and which have stalled. when you wonder whether a muscle is being trained enough in a normal week. when you want the trend for one particular lift, session by session. with the diet coach on and a cut going, to check you are holding your strength while losing weight. step by step open the progress tab. in the your body & training card, tap the strength row. if the training coach is on and you have not logged any sets yet, the row says "log a session to start". read the line under lifts . it says how many of your lifts are up and the median change across them. tap any lift to open its own page. touch the chart and slide your finger along it to read the exact value for any day. go back and look at the sets a week per muscle card. each muscle shows the average number of working sets a week over the last weeks, with a status against the 10-to-20 band described below. warm-up sets never count. for a week-level look across your whole routine, tap the history and reports button (the clock-and-arrow icon) at the top of progress and open sets per muscle . that report shows the hard sets each muscle got this week, and your total working sets per week over the last 8 weeks. how a lift is judged forma takes your best set of the day for a lift and turns it into an estimated one-rep max: the weight you could lift once. it never asks you to test that; the estimate comes from the sets you log. a lift with a load plots one estimated one-rep max per training day, drawn from your best set that day. sets above 12 reps are left out because the formula is unreliable there. a lift with no load, like a hold or bodyweight reps, follows your best hold time or reps in each session instead. the estimate has noise in it, so small day-to-day moves do not count for much. judge the direction over weeks: whether the estimate is higher than it used to be. the percent change next to a lift and the summary line at the top compare recent history rather than everything you have ever logged. lifting heavier today than you did as a beginner years ago does not read as a gain today. how much work a muscle needs the sets-per-week figures use a band that the strength screen spells out: between 10 and 20 working sets a week per muscle grows muscle best, and under 10 is maintenance at most. a set counts when it is not a warm-up. most people build fine anywhere in that range, and the report in sets per muscle shows where a muscle sits. tip: if a lift has not moved for a long run of sessions while the rest are climbing, changing the exercise for that muscle is the usual first thing to try. good to know direction, not decimals. charts, records and changes are estimates, and small changes are inside the noise. read weeks and months, not single sessions. no logging, no trend. everything on this screen comes from sets you log in the train tab, or history you bring in from another app. a lift logged on only one day cannot have a direction yet. warm-ups stay out. warm-up sets never add to your sets per muscle and never affect the estimates. starting the trend. the summary line needs at least two different lifts, each logged on two different days. until then the screen says what to do instead: repeat a lift in two sessions and the trend starts. no test day or special equipment is needed. related log your sets past sessions and reports the fitness score ways to judge progress

title: Tape measurements
summary: Waist, chest, arms and what to compare.
text: tape measurements are a monthly set of six readings with a tape measure: waist, neck, chest, upper arm, thigh and hips. one sitting a month is enough, because a tape does not move fast and what matters is the change between months. when to use it you want a second, independent sign of fat loss while the scale seems stuck. you want to follow arms, thighs or chest over months without new equipment. you have no smart scale and want a way to judge change anyway. you want a reminder so the tape happens each month. step by step on progress, tap the body row, then tape measurements . you can also get there from history & reports , then measurements . tap take your first tape , or add measurements next time. a full tape is all six sites in one sitting, once a month. for each site, the form shows a short instruction underneath. measure and type the number in centimetres; forma reads either a decimal point or a comma. skip any site you could not measure, and save anyway. the entry is kept, but a partial entry does not reset the monthly clock and does not count as this month's full tape. once a site has two or more readings, a chart appears for it. touch the chart and slide your finger along it to read the value on any date. below that, the history list shows your past entries, each labelled "full tape" when all six sites are in it. the six sites each site has a fixed instruction so the next tape measures the same thing: site how to measure waist at the navel, tape level all the way round, at the end of a normal breath out. not pulled tight, not slack. neck just below the larynx, tape sloping slightly down at the front. chest around the fullest part, relaxed. upper arm flexed, midpoint between shoulder and elbow. thigh standing, midway between hip crease and knee. hips at the widest point, feet together. the screen shows each site's instruction while you type, so you do not have to memorise this. what to compare the screen lists your latest reading for each site, next to the change over the last roughly three months. read the direction of that change, not the exact millimetre. compare like with like: same site, same tape, same technique. the instructions exist so that today's waist and next month's waist measure the same thing. the tape's own body-fat estimate waist and neck also give a body-fat estimate, the us navy formula; for women the hips count in it too. the estimate is a second opinion next to your other readings. the scale or a clinic scan is preferred, and the tape estimate never replaces them. when a scale or a clinic scan has answered within the last few weeks, the neck field moves out of the way, because the neck is only needed for the tape's own estimate. a button offers to add it back if you want a full tape. careful: one extra centimetre of slack changes the waist reading more than a month of change can add. keep the tape tension light and level, and note any doubt. good to know the monthly clock. a full tape resets the counter for 28 days. forma tells you where you stand: "no full tape yet", "next full tape in n days", or "a full tape is due. it has been n days." plausible ranges. each field checks a sensible range for the site, for example waist 50-200 cm. a value outside that range is flagged straight away, so a mistyped number does not pollute your trend. tip: turn on monthly tape under reminders in settings for a nudge on a sunday, 28 days after the last one. related body fat and lean mass weight and the 7-day average the fitness score ways to judge progress

title: The Fitness score
summary: What goes into it and how to read it.
text: the fitness score is one number out of 10 that summarises how your training, body and habits have been going lately. it is built from your own logged numbers in forma. progress. when to use it once a week or so, as a slow-moving check that you are heading the right way. when the separate screens give mixed signals and you want the overall picture. when you want to know which one area is holding you back most. when an area has no data yet: the screen says so instead of showing a made-up number. step by step open the progress tab. in the your body & training card, tap the fitness score row. the row appears only once at least one domain has a score; early on it may not be there yet. read the top card: the score out of 10, a band label under it, and one line on how it has moved. look at the four domain cards - fitness , strength , body and behaviours - each with its own score and the areas inside it. open the how this works section on the screen at any time for the rules described below. check weekly snapshots to see the score week by week. one snapshot is saved each week; after the second one, a trend line appears. what goes into it every area is scored 0 to 100 and shown out of 10. each area looks at the last 28 days, and the four domain scores are a plain average of the areas inside them. the headline score is the plain average of the four domains, and all four must have a score before any headline appears. until then the screen says "not enough measured yet" and names which domains it is waiting for. domain areas it averages fitness fitness (vo2 max against what is typical for your age and sex), heart (resting heart rate) strength strength (how your lifts are trending) body body (body fat, or bmi, or a holding note), weight trend (or composition trend from scans) behaviours activity, sleep, nutrition (protein) nothing is weighted or adjusted behind the scenes: the average really is an average. how to read it each area shows either a score with a supporting fact, or a dash with a short "waiting:" line saying exactly what it needs: sleep and protein also use the last 28 days and need at least 7 nights, or 7 logged days, before they count. heart needs a few resting heart rate readings. fitness needs a vo2 max reading, and your age and sex in your profile. strength needs a lift logged on two different days to have a direction. activity needs active-minutes data; from garmin it comes from intensity minutes. weight trend needs a goal set and weigh-ins in the last 4 weeks and in the 4 weeks before, so there is something to compare. body works from a body-fat reading or a clinic scan. if you have neither, it falls back to bmi from your height and recent weigh-ins. an area can also be waiting because a reading is too old. a body-fat reading or clinic scan older than 120 days stops counting and shows as out of date. forma uses your weight pace instead, and prefers a clinic reading over a scale reading when both are recent. the band label sorts scores into strong , good , fair , building and just starting . the body-fat and bmi scores slide smoothly along their scale, so a tenth of a point on your body fat never changes your score by much. good to know it moves slowly on purpose. the last 28 days feed every area, and one snapshot a week is kept. a bad weekend does not dent it; a lost month does. on a cut, holding is winning. when your goal is a cut, keeping your lifts about where they were - down no more than 2% - scores good or better for strength. if your lifts rise, the score rises as usual. outside a cut, strength follows your lift change directly. how change is counted. the three-month change shown with the score counts only areas that had a score at both dates. an area that merely appeared is not an improvement, and one that vanished is not a decline. note: the fitness score is a summary of your own numbers. it is not a medical test and does not replace advice from a doctor. related strength weight and the 7-day average ways to judge progress

title: Your two coaches
summary: The training coach and the diet coach.
text: forma has two coaches: a training coach and a diet coach. each works from your own numbers and does its own job. neither needs the other. when to use it read this page when: you are new to forma and want to know what the two coaches are before you change anything; you want to know whether you must use both. you do not; you want to know what each coach does with your numbers; you have heard that the coaches can notice things together, and want to know what that means. what each coach does the training coach the training coach plans your sessions: which lifts, how many sets, what weight, and when to rest. it progresses your weights over time, calls rest days, and watches your recovery and any injury you log. its work appears on the train tab. the diet coach the diet coach sets your daily calorie and protein target, runs the weekly check, and spots food patterns. it uses your 7-day average weight, not a single weigh-in. its work appears on the fuel tab. both coaches work from what you log: a session, a meal, a weigh-in. neither asks the other for permission, and neither stops working because the other is off. one coach, or both forma starts with both coaches on. if you want only one, you can choose in two places: during setup, tap "i only want the eating coach" on the training-days page, or "only want one coach?" on your plan; any time, open settings > coaches and use the switches. each coach does its own job with its own data. sessions, progression and rest days belong to the training coach. targets and the weekly check belong to the diet coach. only when both coaches are on, and both have data, can they also notice things together. for example: you ate little in a week of heavy training. neither coach could tell you that alone. these extras never replace either coach's own findings, and nothing waits on them. step by step open forma. log your days as usual: a meal, a set, a weigh-in. read the top card on today. it shows what matters most right now: a check-in, a session to start, a weigh-in to add, or a coach finding. prefer only one coach? open settings > coaches and turn the other off. good to know note: both coaches are on from the start. there is nothing to set up. note: the train tab appears when the training coach is on, and the fuel tab when the diet coach is on. turn a coach off and its tab goes with it. note: all numbers come from fixed, tested calculations in the app. any wording you read from a coach is only a description of those numbers. note: forma gives information and estimates, not medical advice. talk to a doctor or another qualified professional about anything medical. related turn a coach on or off what messages to expect your day target, and why it moves

title: Turn a coach on or off
summary: Use only training, only eating, or both.
text: forma has two coaches and you choose which ones you use: the training coach, the diet coach, or both. the switches are in settings > coaches. turning a coach off hides it. nothing you logged is deleted. when to use it you want session plans but no calorie targets, or targets but no session plans. you want to keep logging while the coaching goes quiet for a while. you turned a coach off earlier and want it back. step by step open settings: tap the gear at the top right of today. tap coaches. switch training coach on or off, and diet coach on or off. during setup you can also choose the first time you open forma. the training-days page has "i only want the eating coach", and your plan has "only want one coach?". whatever you pick there, you can change it later in settings > coaches. what each choice changes both on. today shows both areas, and the coaches can also notice things together, such as eating little in a week of heavy training. settings > coaches also shows how they help each other. diet coach only. you get calorie and protein targets. because the diet coach cannot match your training days, the target stays the same every day and is based on how active you usually are. the train tab goes. training coach only. sessions, progression and rest days all work. there are no calorie or protein targets. the fuel tab goes. both off. forma is a plain log. weigh-ins, history and backup still work. there are no targets, session plans, reminders or messages, and today offers to turn a coach back on. in every case: turning a coach off hides its tab, its messages, its reminders, its widget rows and its lines on today. your logs, history and backups are untouched. good to know note: turn a coach back on and its tab, messages and reminders come back, with everything you logged. note: a coach that is off also pauses its reminders. the check-in and injury reminders belong to the training coach; the food, weigh-in, supplements and tape measurement reminders belong to the diet coach. note: with only one coach on, today may show a small card suggesting the other, with one concrete benefit. tap not now and it stays away: it comes back at most once a week, and never after you have dismissed it twice. it never blocks anything. tip: reminder times are chosen under settings > reminders & notifications. related your two coaches what messages to expect the four tabs

title: What messages to expect
summary: When Forma speaks and how to quiet it.
text: forma's coaches speak rarely, never at night, and never the same thing twice while nothing has changed. this page explains what can reach you, how often, and how to make it quieter. when to use it you want to know how often forma will interrupt you. a message arrived and you want to know why. you want fewer messages, or none. you expected a message and none came. how often the coaches speak a coach message is an interruption, so forma limits it. the rules: at most two coach messages in a day. the card on today and a notification count as one message. at least 90 minutes between two. none between 21:00 and 07:00. none in the middle of a session. while a session is open, forma waits. never the same finding twice while nothing has changed. a day with no message is a normal day. you can also see why forma held a message back (see below). what the messages are on today, the top card shows what matters most right now: a check-in, a session to start, a weigh-in to add, or a coach finding. it shows one thing at a time, the most important first. when the coach changes a target, it says why. you can see it under coach decisions in history & reports (the clock button on progress), with an undo where the change can be reversed. reminders are separate from coach messages. a reminder only exists while the thing is still missing: log the meal or the weigh-in and nothing is sent. quieting it turn a coach's messages off open settings, then reminders & notifications. check that ios lets forma reach you. switch the training coach or diet coach messages on or off. a coach can only send when the coach is on, its switch here is on, and ios allows notifications. these switches are about what is delivered to you outside the app. what shows inside forma, such as the card on today, follows the coach switches in settings > coaches instead. on the message itself tap not now to hide it for four weeks, or not useful to hide it for two months. neither changes your targets. tap open fuel, open train or open progress to go to the screen where you can act on it. the next message may take its place. why something was held back settings > coaches has a row called what your coach is considering. it shows what is scheduled, and why each thing was said or held back. if nothing arrives in forma, open settings, then reminders & notifications. the top row says whether ios allows notifications. if it says they are off, tap open ios settings, then notifications, and allow them for forma. also check that the training coach and diet coach switches below it are on. never asked? under reminders & notifications, tap allow notifications. still nothing? check focus and notification summary in ios settings. also remember the limits above: at most two coach messages a day, and only while a coach is on. few messages can mean a quiet week. good to know note: hiding a message does not change your targets. the next message may take the place of one you hid. note: rest is over is a different kind of notification. it comes from the rest timer when your phone is locked or forma is in the background. with forma open you hear two short beeps instead. related your two coaches title: Garmin data
summary: Sleep, recovery and load from your Garmin in your plan.
text: if you wear a garmin watch, forma can bring its sleep, recovery and training numbers into your plan. your watch already measures what happens overnight, so forma reads that instead of asking you to type anything. the training coach weighs it when it plans. garmin data is part of forma power. core works without a watch: your targets, session plans, food logging and the recovery read from your logged sets all run as normal. when to use it you already wear a garmin, and would rather forma read it than enter sleep or rest days by hand. you want the overnight card on today to show your sleep, heart-rate variability (hrv, the variation between your heartbeats) and resting heart rate. you want the readiness and training load from your watch to count toward what the training coach plans next. you hold forma power. without it the garmin screen says "garmin watch data is part of power." and offers see power plans . step by step open settings , then devices , and tap garmin . if the card at the top already reads connected, you are done. otherwise tap connect garmin . a sign-in sheet opens over forma. sign in on garmin's own page inside it. when the sheet closes, the garmin screen says garmin connected. if you stop halfway, it says connecting was cancelled. nothing was changed. wait for your watch to sync with garmin. the screen then shows newest data with the date of the latest reading. before any data arrives it says no data has arrived yet. it appears after your watch syncs. open today . the overnight card shows your sleep, hrv and resting heart rate. the recovery ring fills with the readiness figure from the watch when it sends one, or with the body battery figure when it does not. to stop, tap disconnect garmin on the garmin screen and confirm in the dialog. forma stops receiving data from your watch, and you can connect again whenever you like. note: you can tap check connection on the garmin screen at any time. it asks forma's server what it knows and changes nothing on its own. what your watch adds garmin delivers your data to forma's own server under garmin's open wearables program. forma keeps a copy on the phone, so the numbers are there when you open the app. what it brings: last night's sleep: the time asleep and the sleep score, on the overnight card. hrv and resting heart rate, compared with your own recent nights rather than a general norm. today's stress, breathing and steps on the same card, shown while the newest night on the phone is older than last night. a sleep stage breakdown (deep, light, rem, awake) on the vitals screen in progress. training readiness, training load and your cardio sessions. the training coach reads them when it picks the next session and when it suggests rest. tip: if the numbers look old, the usual reason is a watch that has not uploaded to garmin yet. sync it in garmin's own app, then pull down on today or reopen forma and give it a moment. good to know careful: nothing worked out from your garmin data goes to an online ai service. the garmin screen says: "forma never sends it to online ai." ask coach answers questions about your watch data on the phone. note: connecting goes through forma's server. the server holds the link to your garmin account and knows a connection is active. when garmin's sign-up for new connections is full, the screen says "garmin connections are full right now; try again later." note: you sign in on garmin's own page inside the sheet. forma never sees your garmin password. note: disconnecting does not delete your history. sessions, meals and weigh-ins stay exactly as they are, and the sleep and recovery rows already on the phone are not removed either. note: if your power subscription ends, the garmin screen says paused. garmin data already on this phone stays. no new watch data arrives until you subscribe again. note: forma tells a failed sync apart from old data. if the last sync failed, the overnight card says "garmin sync failed" and keeps showing your last good data. related core and power apple health privacy: what stays where online ai help

title: Online AI help
summary: Food photos and meal descriptions with your consent.
text: online ai help sends a meal photo, or a meal you describe in words, to an online ai service and uses the answer. forma never needs it for your numbers: you log every meal by search, barcode or by hand. nothing goes to an ai service unless you allow it and ask. forma asks once, before anything is sent, and you can switch it off again at any time. when to use it you are eating something with no barcode and no label, and a photo would save you typing. you cooked a one-pan meal and want to describe it in a sentence rather than look up each part. you want coach messages and ask coach answers worded more like a coach would word them. you hold forma power. online ai help is power only: on core, forma contacts no online ai service. step by step on fuel , tap the plus at the top right ( add food ) to open the add food sheet. tap photo , then take photo or choose from library . or tap describe , type what you ate, and tap estimate it . if you have not allowed online ai yet, the online ai help sheet appears first. tap allow , or not now to leave it off. nothing is sent while you read it. the reading runs in the background, about 30 seconds, and you can keep logging. when it is done the card in fuel says ready to check ; tap check . look at what came back: it is a draft, and you can change any part of it. the app adds the totals, not the model. tap save to dinner (the button names the meal you are logging), or discard to drop the estimate and log it another way. later, manage it in settings > ai help : one switch, online ai help . note: search , scan and manual always work. where neither the iphone's own model nor power can do it, those buttons say what is needed and see power opens the plans. note: turning the switch off is immediate and asks no confirmation. it also reaches a photo still waiting to be read: a photo or description that has not been sent stays on your phone and is not sent. you can tap retry later if you allow it again. what the consent sheet says the sheet is titled online ai help . it opens when power becomes active, when you turn the switch on, or on its own just before the first online use. three short lines sit on top: sent: the meal photos and descriptions, and the coach questions, that you ask online ai to read. never sent: your watch data, or anything worked out from it. the third line says an online ai service does the work through forma's own secure server, which keeps nothing, and that you can turn it off any time in settings > ai help. details opens the full text: this is optional, and forma keeps working on your iphone without it. it lists what is sent when you use it: a meal photo or description you ask forma to read, the text you type when you ask the coach, and a substitute request with the exercise and its candidate exercises. it says that your garmin and watch data are never sent, nor your name, your diary or your history. it says that forma reaches the service only through its own secure server, which keeps nothing you send. anything it reads or estimates is a draft you check, while the numbers behind your targets come from your iphone. you can withdraw at any time in settings > ai help . the sheet also links to read the privacy page . forma records which version of this wording you agreed to, so if the text changes it asks again. note: there is one agreement and one switch. you cannot allow photos but not coach wording, or the other way round. good to know note: on an iphone with apple intelligence you may not need the online service at all. apple's model words coach and ask coach answers and estimates meals you describe, all on the phone. it reads photos only where it can see images. it comes with core, and its switch is use the model on this iphone in settings > ai help , on by default where it is available. if your iphone cannot run it, forma uses its own plain wording. limit: the service is asked about food, exercise names and wording. forma does not send it questions about symptoms, pain, medication or a condition: those are answered on the phone with fixed wording, and any wording that strays into medical territory is discarded before you see it. limit: your watch data never goes to the online service, even with online ai help on. ask coach answers questions that draw on watch data on the phone. note: every food estimate, online or on the phone, is one you check. nothing reaches your diary until you tap the save button. related log food: search, scan or by hand core and power privacy: what stays where ask coach

title: Ask Coach
summary: Questions about your own numbers.
text: ask coach answers questions about your own training and eating from what you have logged. you ask in your own words. forma reads your log on the phone, works the numbers out there, and gives you the answer. ask coach is part of forma power. everyone sees the speech-bubble button on today: without power it opens the plans instead of the sheet. when to use it you want to read your own numbers without going through each tab: what you did last session, how many sets you did this week, how many calories you have left today. you want one number explained, such as why your target is what it is. you want to know how a lift is going, or whether a food fits your day. you hold forma power. step by step on today , tap the speech-bubble button next to the settings gear at the top right. the sheet opens as ask coach . type your question in the ask a question box and tap the arrow to send, or tap one of the try asking chips for a question forma suggests. while it works, a card says let me check your logs… and the answer appears in place of it. read the answer. every number in it is picked out (heavier type, in forma's accent colour). why this answer opens a list of which of your figures were used and where each came from. the app says: "every number above is worked out by the app from your own logs. none comes from a language model." if the answer points at a screen to act on, an arrow button opens it: open fuel , open train , open progress or open settings . tap close when you are done. note: if your power has ended while the sheet is open, the bar at the bottom changes to ask coach is part of power , with "your power subscription has ended, so ask is paused. subscribe again to use it." tip: nothing you ask or read is kept, so there is no conversation history when you come back. good to know note: the coach does the maths before any wording. your logged data produces the answer on the phone, and an online ai service only shapes how the answer is phrased. it never sees your watch data. note: if online ai help is off, forma keeps answering from your logs in its own words. turning it on (settings > ai help) can make the same answers read more like a coach's voice. limit: there is a limit on how long one question can be, and on how many you can send in a row. near the length limit the box counts your characters, and if you send too much too soon forma says so. note: questions about symptoms, pain, medication, pregnancy or a medical condition get a fixed reply. it points you to a doctor or another qualified professional instead of an answer. questions about self-harm, or about food or your body weighing on you, get a fixed reply that helps you find support, with a find a helpline link. safety replies are settled on the phone and are never sent away to be reworded. note: if one of your coaches is switched off, the questions that need it are answered with a short note, such as "the training coach is off, so i cannot answer training questions.", plus a button that opens settings > coaches. note: a question about how to use a feature is answered from forma's built-in help. that uses none of your data. related core and power online ai help your two title: iCloud backup and restore
summary: Your own private iCloud, and what to do if it is off.
text: forma keeps a copy of your data in your own private icloud, and keeps the previous copy too. a lost phone or a mistake does not cost you your history. everything works with no connection, and the backup catches up when you are back online. when to use it you want to check that your data is being backed up, or run a backup now. you have a new iphone and want to bring your history with you. you deleted something by mistake and want to go back to an earlier copy. forma shows a small dot on the gear at the top of today. it appears when backups have failed or been missing for three days. step by step to check or run a backup open forma, then open settings. tap data & backup . read the icloud status line. it says whether you are backed up and when, or what is in the way. if you want a backup now, tap back up now . the status line can say: on · last backed up [time] — the last backup succeeded. everything on this phone as of that moment is safe in icloud. backing up… — forma is copying a snapshot to icloud right now. on · waiting for a connection — everything is saved on this phone. the backup runs the next time you are online. on · not backed up yet — your first backup runs on its own the next time you open forma, or tap back up now. icloud is full — this appears as a message under the status line: there is no room left in your icloud storage for the backup. your data is safe on the phone. free up space in settings > apple account > icloud and forma will carry on. careful: if icloud already holds a fuller copy than this phone, forma will not overwrite it. it says so and offers two choices: replace the backup with this phone's data , or keep the backup as it is . choose with care; if the backup is right, restore from it instead. to restore on a new phone install forma and sign in to the same apple account. on the first screen, tap restoring a backup? . tap restore from icloud . forma downloads the latest copy; the screen says how many records were downloaded when it is done. force-quit and reopen forma. the restored data is now in place. if forma is already installed (no first screen), open settings, tap data & backup , then restore from backup . to restore an earlier copy open settings, then data & backup , then restore from backup . choose either latest backup or earlier copy . each row shows its date and how many entries it holds. tap download and apply at next launch . force-quit and reopen forma. note: nothing changes until you restart forma. you get a message when the download is done, telling you how many entries were prepared. good to know your data lives on this phone. the copy in icloud is yours, in your own icloud account. forma works with no connection; the backup catches up when you are back online. restoring replaces what is on the iphone with what is in that backup. anything logged since then is replaced. your current data is kept aside, not deleted. the earlier copy is the backup from before the latest one. it is kept so that one bad backup cannot leave you without copies. forma never overwrites a fuller backup by itself. if a backup is refused, the app asks you which side is right. offline is a normal state. if the backup cannot reach icloud, forma says so and tries again later. limit: if your iphone is not signed in to icloud, backups cannot run until you sign in. your data is still saved on the phone. if a backup message says icloud is off, see the next steps: sign in to icloud to back up: open the ios settings app, sign in with your apple account, then return to forma and tap back up now. icloud is turned off for forma: icloud is restricted on this phone, often by screen time or a device-management profile. ask whoever manages the phone. icloud is full: free up space in settings > apple account > icloud. your data stays safe on the phone. "can't check icloud right now" or "icloud is busy": temporary. forma tries again the next time you open it. related export or delete all my data privacy: what stays where troubleshooting setting up

title: Apple Health
summary: What Forma reads and what stays on the phone.
text: forma can read your weight, body fat and lean mass, and your daily activity, from apple health. if your smart scale writes to health, its readings arrive in forma without you typing anything. forma only reads from health. it never writes to it. when to use it you use a smart scale that writes your weigh-ins to apple health, and you want them to show up in forma by themselves. you track steps or daily activity elsewhere and want forma to use them. you want forma to read sleep, heart-rate or heart-rate-variability readings from your watch to help plan training and recovery. you want to change or stop what forma reads. step by step to connect open forma, then open settings. tap devices . tap apple health . tap allow apple health and choose what to share in the health access screens that follow. once connected, the row says connected and shows when forma last synced. weigh-ins from your scale arrive as they happen. to read sleep, hrv and resting heart rate on the same apple health screen, find the section sleep, hrv and resting heart rate . tap use sleep and heart data . choose what to share in the health screens that follow. this part is separate from weight and body measurements. if your watch writes those readings to health, forma can use them to plan training and recovery. they stay on your phone and in your own icloud backup. to pull in new readings by hand on the apple health screen, tap check now . you rarely need this. new readings arrive on their own while you use the app. good to know readings from health count as weigh-ins on the weight page, where the 7-day average is what matters. a single reading is one point. on the apple health screen there is a switch, pause reading from health . while paused, forma reads nothing new from health. what is already on this phone stays. unpause to read again. you can also turn the connection off altogether in the health app, under settings > health > data access & devices > forma . if the status says no readings yet , either forma's access is off in the health app, or your scale or watch has not written readings to health yet. health does not tell apps which, so check both. activity can be granted separately. if the apple health screen offers also allow activity , tap it to let forma read daily activity too. if sleep and heart readings still do not appear, a request has to be made from inside forma: tap use my watch data on the overnight card on today, or the use sleep and heart data button on the apple health screen. health shows its permission sheet only when an app makes such a request. note: health does not tell forma whether access is granted. it also does not tell forma when you turn access back off. if readings stop arriving, check the switch above and the data access & devices list in the health app. limit: on devices without health data, this screen says "not available on this iphone" and nothing can be connected. related weight and the 7-day average icloud backup title: Export or delete all my data
summary: JSON and CSV, and a clean delete.
text: export gives you a copy of everything you entered or connected in forma, as files, to keep or to use somewhere else. delete wipes forma clean, either on this phone alone or together with the icloud backup, and sends you back to the first-run screen. you find both at the bottom of settings > data & backup . when to use it you want a copy of your whole history to hold yourself, or to take to another tool. you are moving to a new phone and also want a copy beyond the icloud backup. you want to start over with an empty forma. you are finishing with forma, or handing the phone to someone else. step by step export all my data open forma, then open settings. tap data & backup . tap export all my data . a message shows "preparing your export…" while the file is built. when it is ready, the standard ios share sheet opens. choose where the files go: for example save to files , or airdrop to another device. what you get is one export file: everything in it, as json, plus lists of your food, workouts and weight as csv files you can open as spreadsheets. tip: export before you delete. exporting first gives you a copy; after a delete there is nothing left to export. delete all my data in settings > data & backup , tap delete all my data… . a first question, "delete all your data?", asks you to confirm. tap continue to move on, or cancel to stop. a second step asks again, with a heading that says plainly: this cannot be undone. it offers two buttons, delete from this phone and icloud and delete from this phone only . choose the one you want. forma removes your profile, meals, workouts, weigh-ins and settings from this phone and shows an "everything was deleted" summary of what is gone. tap ok and settings closes. forma then shows its first-run screen. good to know the icloud backup is a separate copy. if you choose "delete from this phone only", your backup stays in your icloud, so you can restore later on this or another phone. if you choose "delete from this phone and icloud", that backup is deleted too. if you use forma power, deleting everything also removes your online forma account: your garmin connection, your registered phones, this phone's key and your online ai permission. if the app could not remove the online account because there was no connection, it says so and offers a try again button. the export covers what you typed and what forma computed, from the data on this phone. meal photos, and data synced from a server you set up yourself, are not included. you do not need to delete everything for a fresh start with your plan. changing coaches, training or diet goals is in settings, and none of it touches your history. careful: deleting cannot be undone. export first if you want a copy. limit: apple health keeps its own data. deleting in forma does not change anything in the health app, and the permission for forma there also stays until you change it in health. note: "everything was deleted" lists what is gone, in plain words: what was removed from this phone, whether the online account (if any) went with it, and whether the icloud backup was deleted or kept, so you can restore later. related icloud backup and title: Privacy: what stays where
summary: On the phone, in your iCloud, and what Power sends.
text: forma keeps your data on your phone, with a backup copy in your own icloud. this page lists every place your data can go, so you know what leaves the phone, when, and why. when to use it you want to know where your meals, workouts and weigh-ins are stored, and who can see them. you are wondering what a food search or barcode scan sends out. you are deciding whether to switch on the optional forma power extras, and want to know what they send. you want to check that nothing tracks you or feeds advertising. what stays on the phone everything you enter or connect stays in the app's database on this phone: your profile (height, birth date, sex, goal), weigh-ins, body measurements, meals and foods you saved, workouts and sets, supplements, injuries you log, check-in notes, targets and settings. the developer cannot see any of it and does not receive it. that includes apple health. forma reads your weight, body fat and lean mass from health only if you allow it, so a smart-scale reading arrives without typing. forma never writes to health, and health data is never sent to forma, to anyone else, or to the online ai service. barcode scanning also runs on the phone, using apple's scanner. the camera is used only while the scanning screen is open; nothing is recorded or kept. note: there is no forma account to create and no sign-in. forma does not track you, has no advertising and uses no analytics services. what goes to your icloud in forma core, the only copy of your data that leaves the phone is the backup. it goes to a private area of your own icloud, tied to your apple account, so only you can read it. forma keeps the latest backup and the one before it, so an earlier copy always remains. if you allow apple health, your weigh-ins can arrive on the phone by themselves. they are still stored only on the phone and in that backup. what a food lookup sends looking up a food sends the words you typed, or the barcode digits, to open food facts, a public nutrition database, over a secure connection. no name, account or device identifier goes with it. the bundled usda table works entirely on the phone, with no connection at all. what forma power sends forma power is optional, and nothing goes online until you allow it. two things use forma's own server: watch connection (garmin). your watch's sleep, heart-rate variability, activities and weight arrive from garmin through forma's server. watch data is never sent to the ai service. online ai help. the meal photo or typed meal description you send to be read, the text you type when you ask the coach, and any exercise-substitute request go through forma's server to an online ai service. your watch data is never sent to it. forma keeps none of what you send: no photo, no text. to confirm your subscription, the server also receives the signed purchase record from apple, together with the device token it issued when forma registered this phone. these are used only to keep power working. they are never used for tracking, and the same is true of everything above: the app store's own privacy summary lists them because they leave the phone. each one exists to provide the feature you asked for; nothing is used for any other purpose. good to know turning off online ai help stops the sending at once, even for photos still waiting to be read. you can see and change what forma may read from apple health at any time in the health app. settings > data & backup shows the state of the backup in a few words, and offers back up now , export all my data and delete all my data . deleting all your data removes it from the phone, and offers to delete the icloud backup too. related icloud backup and restore export or delete all my data apple health online ai help

title: About, and not medical advice
summary: What Forma is and is not.
text: forma logs your training and your eating, and works out your targets, sessions and rest days from the numbers you enter or connect. this page says what forma is, what it is not, and where to find the version, legal pages and credits. when to use it you want to know what the numbers in forma are, and how far you can trust them. you have a health condition and want to know whether forma is right for you. you are looking for the app's version number, its privacy policy or terms of use, or a way to contact support. you want to know where the food data and pictures in the app come from. what forma is forma gives information and suggestions, not medical advice. your calorie and protein targets, the training sessions it plans, its recovery notes and the fitness score are all estimates. they are calculated from the numbers you enter or connect and general fitness rules, so they can be wrong for you: the calculation is only as good as its inputs. forma is not a medical device. it does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any condition. the supplements list records what you take and what it adds. forma never tells you what to take or how much. the injury planner only avoids and swaps lifts; it does not judge how an injury should be treated. for supplements, ask a doctor or pharmacist. for an injury, follow your physio or doctor. talk to a professional first talk to a doctor or another qualified professional before you change how you eat or train, especially if any of these apply to you: you are pregnant or breastfeeding. you are under 18. you are injured or recovering from one. you take medication. you have a medical condition or an eating disorder. if something hurts or feels wrong while you train, stop. in an emergency, call your local emergency number. finding about, and the legal pages at the bottom of settings, about & help shows the app's version and links to: privacy policy — what data stays on your phone, what goes to your icloud, and what leaves it. terms of use — the agreement between you and forma. contact support — where to ask a question or report a problem. the same screen lists not medical advice , which repeats the summary above. where the data in forma comes from food data comes from usda fooddata central, bundled in the app, and from open food facts, looked up when you scan a barcode or search for a food. it may contain errors. check the label when a package has one. acknowledgements (in settings) lists where the food data, the exercise pictures and other material in forma come from. good to know note: the developer holds none of your data. to see, correct or remove it, use export all my data and delete all my data in settings > data & backup. limit: the estimates in forma are a starting point, not a prescription. check them against your own results over weeks. if the scale disagrees with a target for long enough, question the target. related privacy: what stays where what forma is for the fitness score injuries

title: A barcode is not found
summary: What to do when the scanner finds nothing.
text: sometimes a scan reads the bars cleanly and forma still cannot log the food. this page explains what each message means and the quickest way to log the meal anyway. when to use it the scanner read the bars, but forma says the barcode is not in the database. open food facts knows the product but has no nutrition figures for it. the lookup could not finish because the food database could not be reached. the camera will not start at all, so there is nothing to scan with. step by step tap enter it by hand on the message. type the food's name, the grams, and the protein, carbs and fat from the label. check the numbers, then save. or tap search instead and search for the food by name in search foods . tap a result. change the grams if you need to, check the numbers, and save. tip: if the bars will not read at all, type the digits printed under the bars into the digits under the bars field and tap look up . a barcode has 6 to 14 digits. look up waits until you have typed at least 6 digits. if the entry is too long or has anything but digits, forma says so instead of searching. what each message means "that barcode isn't in open food facts." the product is missing from the public database. enter it by hand once, and the next scan finds it. where meal photos can be read (apple intelligence on iphones that support it, or forma power), the message says "that barcode isn't in the database" instead. it adds that a photo of the label is read for the numbers but does not keep the barcode; only a hand entry keeps it. "open food facts knows this product but has no nutrition figures for it." the product exists in the database, but without usable numbers. enter them by hand from the label. "couldn't reach open food facts." the phone is offline or the database did not answer. nothing is broken: your own foods and the bundled usda table still work, and scanning works again when you are back online. after a lookup that could not finish, forma does not keep the digits; when you are online again, scan once more or type them in. "that doesn't look like a barcode (6 to 14 digits)." the digits you typed were not a plausible barcode. check for a missed digit or a letter that slipped in. good to know enter it by hand opens the same form as manual . forma works out the calories from the protein, carbs and fat you type, and you see the numbers before anything is saved. a hand entry made after a scan keeps the barcode with the food, as long as the entry is one food. the next scan of that package finds it in your own library straight away, even with no signal. in search foods , your own foods come first, then the bundled usda table, then packaged foods from open food facts. a scan checks your own foods first (instant, works with no signal), then open food facts. a result never saves itself. whatever a scan finds lands on the confirm sheet first, where you check the portion and the numbers. scanning runs entirely on your phone with apple's barcode scanner. the camera is used only while the scanning screen is open; nothing is recorded or kept. only the barcode itself, or the words you type in a food search, goes out to open food facts. if the camera has not been allowed yet, the scan pane shows allow the camera to scan with a button to allow it. if the camera is turned off for forma in ios settings, it shows that with an open settings button. on a device that cannot scan barcodes, it asks you to type the digits instead. where meal photos can be read, photographing a product's nutrition label ( photograph its label ) reads the numbers, which you check before saving. it does not attach the barcode. use enter it by hand if you want the next scan of that package to find the food. related log food: search, scan or by hand ways to log your food troubleshooting saved meals and repeating a meal
